title: Podio AI & MCP Podio MCP Server Integration Guide - Progress Podio
snippet:
The Podio MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server connects AI assistants — **ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Claude Desktop**, and any other MCP-compatible platform — directly to your Podio data. Once connected, your AI assistant can read and write your Podio workspaces, apps, and items using plain natural language.
**No coding required to get started**. The server is live at **[https://mcp.podio.com](https://mcp.podio.com)** — just point your AI platform at it and log in with your Podio account.

The Podio MCP Server gives your AI assistant 22 tools covering both reading and writing your Podio data:
| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| Browse | List organizations, workspaces, apps, and members |
| Read data | Fetch items with full field values, filter and search across your account |
| Write data | Create and update items, post comments |
| Tasks | Create, update, reassign, and complete tasks |
| Notifications | Read recent activity and notifications |

The server uses **shared default credentials** so you can connect immediately without creating a Podio API key. You simply log in with your Podio account when prompted.
**Recommended for:** VSCode / GitHub Copilot and any platform where you cannot enter your own API credentials. Also fine for trying the integration before committing to your own API key.
The setup depends on your AI platform — jump to the Connect Your AI Platform section for step-by-step instructions. The key things to know:
- **MCP Server URL:** `https://mcp.podio.com/mcp`
- **Authorization URL:** `https://mcp.podio.com/oauth/authorize`
- **Token URL:** `https://mcp.podio.com/oauth/token`
- **No client ID or secret needed** when using default credentials.
The first time you connect, your AI platform will open a browser window where you log into Podio and click **Allow access**. After that, your AI assistant is ready to use.

#### Option B — With your own Podio API key (recommended)
Follow the steps above for “Using your Own API Key” first, then use your **Client ID** and **Client Secret** in the fields below.
1. Create Blank Agent
2. Go to the tools section
3. Add a new **Model Context Protocol** tool
4. Enter **Name, Description**
5. For Server URL, use [https://mcp.podio.com](https://mcp.podio.com)
6. Select **OAuth 2.0** with **Manual Type**
7. Enter your **Client ID** and **Client Secret** you created in Podio.
8. Enter the following details for mandatory Fields Values:
- **MCP Server URL:** `https://mcp.podio.com/mcp`
- **Authorization

title: Getting started with Podia MCP
snippet:
**Podia MCP** is a Model Context Protocol server that connects your Podia account to AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT.
Once connected, you can ask the AI to browse products, search contacts, draft email broadcasts, create content, and more, all from a single conversation.
# What's an MCP?
An MCP, or **Model Context Protocol**, is an open standard that lets AI tools securely connect to external apps and services. An MCP server acts as a bridge between the AI and a connected service, allowing the AI to access information and perform supported actions based on your instructions.
With Podia MCP, you can ask an AI tool to work with your Podia account, such as browsing products, searching contacts, drafting email broadcasts, creating content, and more.

Using Podia MCP involves three steps:
1. **Ask:** Describe what you want to accomplish in plain language.
2. **Build:** Podia MCP finds information, completes supported actions, or creates content based on your request.
3. **Review:** Open your Podia Admin dashboard to review any drafts or changes before publishing.
For example, instead of filtering your audience, reviewing course progress, and drafting a promotional email separately, you could ask:
*“Find everyone who completed my Photography Fundamentals course. Create a 20% discount coupon for my Advanced Photography course. Then draft an email with the subject ‘Take your photography skills further’ explaining that these students can use the coupon to enroll in the advanced course."*
Podia MCP finds the matching contacts, creates the coupon, and prepares the email draft. You can then review the results in your Admin dashboard before sending the email or publishing the coupon.

title: How to integrate Podio with Hermes
snippet:
**1. Get your MCP URL and API Key**
Go to [dashboard.composio.dev](https://dashboard.composio.dev/login?utm_source=toolkits&utm_medium=framework_template&utm_campaign=hermes&utm_content=api_key&next=%2F~%2Forg%2Fconnect%2Fclients%2Fhermes) and copy your Connect MCP URL and API key.

**2. Open the Hermes config file**
bash
```
nano ~/.hermes/config.yaml
```
**3. Add the Composio Connect MCP server**
bash
```
mcp_servers:
composio:
url: "https://connect.composio.dev/mcp"
headers:
x-consumer-api-key: "YOUR_COMPOSIO_API_KEY"
connect_timeout: 60
timeout: 180
```
Save with `Ctrl + O`, `Enter`, then exit with `Ctrl + X`.

The Podio MCP server is an implementation of the Model Context Protocol that connects your AI agent and assistants like Claude, Cursor, etc directly to your Podio account. It provides structured and secure access to your Podio apps, workspaces, items, tasks, comments, and organization data, so your agent can create and find work items, manage tasks, organize app workflows, and coordinate team activity on your behalf.
- **App and workspace management:** Have your agent find app details, create apps and fields, activate or deactivate apps, and create or archive workspaces.
- **Item and workflow management:** Let the agent create, clone, filter, calculate, export, and delete items across your Podio apps.
- **Task coordination:** Direct your agent to create tasks, assign them to users, add labels and due dates, mark tasks complete, or remove tasks that are no longer needed.
- **Team collaboration:** Instruct your agent to add comments to Podio items and tasks, attach files or links, and remove comments when needed.
- **Organization administration:** Have your agent create organizations, look up administered organizations, manage organization spaces and member roles, and end organization memberships.

With a standalone Podio MCP server, the agents and LLMs can only access a fixed set of Podio tools tied to that server. However, with the Composio Tool Router, agents can dynamically load tools from Podio and many other apps based on the task at hand, all through a single MCP endpoint.
###
Yes, you can. Hermes fully supports MCP integration. You get structured tool calling, message history handling, and model orchestration while Tool Router takes care of discovering and serving the right Podio tools.

title: @forumviriumhelsinki/podio-mcp
snippet:
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that integrates Podio with Claude, enabling natural language management of Podio items and tasks. Automate workflows, manage projects, and organize work with conversational AI.
## Features
- **OAuth2 Authentication** - Secure authentication with automatic token refresh
- **CRUD Operations** - Create, read, update, and delete Podio items and tasks
- **Intelligent Caching** - App structure caching with automatic refresh for performance
- **AI-Powered Suggestions** - Smart project/epic suggestions using fuzzy matching
- **Multi-Workspace Support** - Works with any Podio workspace using explicit coordinates
- **Comprehensive Search** - Search items, tasks, files, and conversations across scopes
- **Notification Management** - Manage and filter Podio notifications
- **Activity Tracking** - Full comment and revision history for items
- **File Attachments** - Upload local files and attach them to items or comments
- **Robust Error Handling** - Detailed error messages for debugging
## Tech Stack
| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| **Runtime** | Node.js 24+ / Bun |
| **Language** | TypeScript 5.9+ |
| **Protocol** | Model Context Protocol SDK ^0.7.0 |
| **Testing** | Jest 30 |
| **Code Quality** | Biome 2.3+ (linting & formatting) |
| **Documentation** | TypeDoc |
| **Package Manager** | npm / Bun |

### Configure
Add to your MCP client configuration (`.mcp.json` or Claude Desktop config):
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"podio-mcp": {
"command": "bunx",
"args": ["@forumviriumhelsinki/podio-mcp"],
"env": {
"PODIO_CLIENT_ID": "${PODIO_CLIENT_ID}"
}
}
}
}
```
This uses Podio's implicit OAuth flow, which only needs a Client ID. To use the auth-code flow instead, add `PODIO_CLIENT_SECRET` to the `env` block. `PODIO_REDIRECT_URI` is optional — the package defaults to `http://localhost:8080/callback`; override it only if your Podio app is registered with a different redirect URI.

title: Podio MCP Server
snippet:
# Podio MCP Server
An MCP server for the Podio API. Any MCP client can list, create, read, update, delete and search Podio items, comments, webhooks and files.

The stdio transport is the default mode, for MCP clients that launch the server locally.
**1. Create `.env` from the template:**
```bash
cp .env.example .env
```
**2. Fill in the required environment variables:**
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `PODIO_CLIENT_ID` | From your Podio API key page (Settings > API Keys) |
| `PODIO_CLIENT_SECRET` | From your Podio API key page |
| `PODIO_REDIRECT_URI` | Must be exactly `http://localhost:8888/callback` |
| `PODIO_TOKEN_PATH` | Token file location (default: `.podio-tokens.json`) |
Leave `MCP_TRANSPORT` empty or unset for stdio mode.
**3. Authenticate:**
```bash
npm run auth
```
This opens a browser window, completes the OAuth2 flow (including Google SSO), and saves tokens to the path specified by `PODIO_TOKEN_PATH`.
**4. Build:**
```bash
npm run build
```
**5. Register with your MCP client:**
Most clients take a JSON config like this:
```json
{
"mcpServers": {
"podio": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/absolute/path/to/podio-mcp-server/dist/index.js"],
"env": {
"PODIO_CLIENT_ID": "your_client_id",
"PODIO_CLIENT_SECRET": "your_client_secret",
"PODIO_REDIRECT_URI": "http://localhost:8888/callback",
"PODIO_TOKEN_PATH": "/absolute/path/to/podio-mcp-server/.podio-tokens.json"
}
}
}
}
```
Replace `/absolute/path/to` with the actual path to your clone.

## Architecture
```
MCP client
│
▼
MCP Protocol (stdio or Streamable HTTP)
│
▼
podio-mcp-server
├── src/server.ts ← 20 tool registrations (Zod schemas)
├── src/auth/ ← OAuth2 flow + token manager
├── src/client/ ← Axios interceptors, rate limiting
├── src/types/ ← Podio API type definitions
└── src/utils/ ← Error handling, logging (stderr)
│
▼
Podio REST API (api.podio.com)
```
**Key design decisions:**
- OAuth2 authorization code flow — supports Google SSO (App auth does not)
- Automatic token refresh with 8-hour TTL
- All logging to stderr — stdout reserved for JSON-RPC over stdio
- Rate limit metadata included in every tool response (`_meta.rate_limit_remaining`)
- Stateless per-request HTTP transport for EC2 deployment (no session state needed)

title: Podio MCP Server by phases
snippet:
# Podio MCP Server
# Podio MCP Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Podio. Inspect APIs, authenticate, manage items/tasks/apps, and generate TypeScript field configs from Cursor, Claude Desktop, or any MCP-compatible client.
## Features
- **Consolidated Podio tools** — items, apps/spaces, tasks, communication, search, metadata, system
- **Generic API caller** — call any catalogued Podio endpoint via `callPodioApi`
- **OAuth / app-token auth** — organization- and app-level tokens
- **API catalog** — browse and search Podio endpoints
- **HTTP/SSE mode** — optional remote access (Docker / `npm run start:http`)
Related MCP server: [Taskade MCP Server](/mcp/servers/tongchai00/mcp)

Cursor, Claude Desktop)
## Quick start (npm / npx)
Add to your MCP client config (e.g. Cursor `.cursor/mcp.json`):
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"podio-developer-mcp": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "@phasesdk/mcp-server-for-podio"]
}
}
}
```
Create `podio.config.json` in the **working directory** the client uses for the server (often your project root):
```
cp podio.config.json.example podio.config.json
# edit clientId, clientSecret, apps
```
Restart the client, then verify with `podio_system` operation `ping` or `get_config_status`.
## Install from source
```
git clone https://github.com/phases/mcp-server-for-podio.git
cd mcp-server-for-podio
npm install
npm run build
```
Point the client at the built entry:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"podio-developer-mcp": {
"command": "node",
"args": ["/absolute/path/to/mcp-server-for-podio/dist/index.js"]
}
}
}
```

HTTP mode (landing page + SSE):
```
npm run start:http
# open http://localhost:3016/
```
## Available tools
| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `podio_items` | Get, create, update, delete, filter items; field history / revisions |
| `podio_apps_spaces` | Orgs, spaces, apps, streams |
| `podio_tasks` | Get, list, create, update, complete tasks |
| `podio_communication` | Comments, statuses, notifications, tags, subscriptions |
| `podio_search` | Global / app search and contacts |
| `podio_metadata` | API catalog, app fields, app relations (incl. deep / CRM map), forms, views |
| `podio_system` | `ping`, `get_config_status`, field config generation, files, hooks, batch, calendar |
| `callPodioApi` | Call any endpoint from the bundled API catalog |

## Deploy (HTTP / remote MCP)
Use this when clients connect over a URL (SSE), not local `npx`/stdio.
